method_specification.methodology_stated_.reason: Motif results appear in Section 4.2, while the uncertainty model and calibration protocol are first fully formulated in Sections 5.1–5.2. The motif Methodology subsection also leaves important assignment and selection details to code.

method_specification.motif_methodology_c.reason: The paper explains geometry-based features, discovery scanning, and tree settings, but does not specify all bond-order thresholds, motif predicates, or numerical inclusion criteria. Reproduction requires the code, including coverage 0.1–60%, q<0.05, and failure-rate ratio ≥1.25.

method_specification.uncertainty_model_c.reason: The five input signals, log-linear score, least-squares fitting target, discovery-only fitting, and isotonic mapping to absolute error are explicitly defined. method_specification.calibration_protoco.reason: The protocol specifies a disjoint discovery/validation split, uncertainty deciles, bin-weighted absolute ECE, the >1 kcal/mol failure definition, and the uncertainty operating threshold of 1 kcal/mol. The code defines the threshold sweep and tie handling.

method_specification.hipnn_architecture_.reason: The headline architecture and optimizer values are specified, but the required matching training protocol is not fully reproduced. In particular, the implemented L2 loss omits the source paper's energy-readout weight penalty, so the stated faithful-protocol condition is unmet.

method_specification.motivation_grounded.reason: The method is connected to ensembles, Bayesian and dropout uncertainty, learned error estimators, and conformal prediction, including post-2018 citations. Positioning remains mostly brief family-level comparisons; the closest chemistry-based failure-analysis literature receives a generic, uncited description.

two_baseline_reporting.paper_as_reported.reason: Table 1 includes explicitly labeled paper rows for 110,426 and 50,000 molecules, with Table I references and MAEs 0.256±0.003 and 0.354±0.004 kcal/mol.

two_baseline_reporting.reimplemented_row.reason: The reimplemented row identifies the ≤8-heavy-atom training subset, 20,799 training molecules, and the submitted three-seed test MAE of 0.803±0.009 kcal/mol.

two_baseline_reporting.paper_as_reported.reason: The published accuracy and tail-error values have specific Table I/Table II locations, and the reference ledger also identifies the relevant figure, equations, architecture, and training-protocol sections.

two_baseline_reporting.reimplementation_.reason: The main runs' in-distribution validation MAE averages 0.311686 kcal/mol, below the nearest 50k reference of 0.354 despite less training data. baseline_verification.reimpl_run_on_le8_.reason: The three main runs document the heavy-atom partition, 20,799 training and 1,000 validation molecules, configurations, split indices, and completed execution. Saved train and validation heavy-atom counts are all ≤8.

baseline_verification.held_fixed_archite.reason: The model retains the required 2 interactions, 3 on-site layers, 80 features, 20 sensitivities, batch size 30, and main optimizer settings. experimental_completeness.seed_count.reason: Three independently initialized and shuffled main HIP-NN runs completed at the required architecture. Their validation partitions differ, and all have final execution records and evaluated checkpoints.

experimental_completeness.full_test_set_.reason: The retained inventory contains 130,823 molecules, including 109,024 with nine heavy atoms. Each seed's evaluation contains exactly these 109,024 unique test identifiers, with no omissions.

experimental_completeness.motif_assignme.reason: All nine motif flag arrays contain 109,024 entries aligned with the complete test inventory. Overlap is explicitly acknowledged and cumulative attribution uses unions rather than double-counting.

reimplementation_accuracy.mae_matches_or.reason: The in-distribution ≤8-heavy validation comparison clears the nearest reference, but the reported 50k anchor does not meet the strict floor across every reported training size: its mean MAE is 0.358039 versus 0.354 kcal/mol, a 1.14% gap. Overlapping error bars do not satisfy an at-or-below target. The 0.803 OOD MAE is not treated as a comparable in-distribution reproduction result.

conformational_transfer.test_executed_qu.reason: A substantial-sized ANI-1x sample of 60,000 conformations was evaluated with all nine motifs and downstream discussion. However, the purported offset removal centers absolute errors, not signed residuals, so it is not invariant to the energy-reference offset. On the saved data, absolute-error centering gives 19.0969 kcal/mol, while signed-residual centering within the same groups gives 29.1701; 566 groups contain both residual signs. This limits the scientific validity of the claimed conformational transfer.

failure_motif_identification.motif_count.reason: Nine operational motifs span ring topology and molecular shape, electronic/functional-group chemistry, and steric contacts. Each has quantitative held-out support; even the smallest validation group contains 58 molecules.

failure_motif_identification.statistical.reason: The saved confirmatory statistics provide every motif's coverage, matching and non-matching error means, medians and 90th percentiles, Mann–Whitney p-values, and Fisher tests. failure_motif_identification.motif_defin.reason: All nine motifs have deterministic code predicates, including shared-ring bonds, ring counts, conjugated-link counts, functional-group tests, radius of gyration <2.2 Å, and non-bonded H–H distance <1.9 Å. The supporting geometry and bond-perception rules are included.

uncertainty_calibration.calibration_curv.reason: All ten held-out combined-model bins lie within ±10% of identity. The largest relative deviation from the mean predicted value is approximately 7.85%; the full decile range is included.

uncertainty_calibration.ece_reported.reason: The reported combined-model ECE is 0.018 kcal/mol, corresponding to the logged 0.0177437, below 0.05. The normalized metric is also reported, at 0.0281772.

uncertainty_calibration.precision_recall.reason: The released analysis reports 33 distinct combined-model sweep thresholds and a justified operating point at predicted error >1 kcal/mol. At that point, held-out precision is 57.97% and recall 57.10%; the paper explains its chemical-accuracy rationale.

motif_compactness.pareto_analysis_qualit.reason: The first four motifs cover 80.2338% of all 10,695 primary-seed validation failures, satisfying K≤5 and ≥80%. The complete library covers 81.1781%, with overlap removed by set union.

mechanism_analysis.subsection_present.reason: Section 4.3 is explicitly devoted to where the hierarchy fails and includes a per-motif hierarchy figure.

mechanism_analysis.depth.reason: The analysis quantitatively connects structural motifs to second-order contributions and R2, and distinguishes delocalized failures with relatively normal hierarchies. Explanations remain grouped and partly observational: for example, nitro is identified as a 13-fold second-order outlier with heteroatom localization, without explaining which chemical property makes its hierarchy fail. A complete mechanistic account for every motif is not established.

failure_analysis.subsection_present.reason: The dedicated section 'What the motif library misses' addresses both uncovered failures and uncertainty-model failures.

failure_analysis.uncovered_molecules_add.reason: The analysis identifies 2,013 uncovered validation failures, 18.82% of all validation failures, and characterizes their heteroatom enrichment, lower ring counts, absent aromaticity, and milder errors relative to covered failures.

failure_analysis.uncertainty_failures_ad.reason: Both failure types are discussed with chemical-class examples: inflated but accurately predicted fused-ring systems as false positives, and quiet delocalization or heteroatom-rich failures as false negatives. The discussion connects these to hierarchy signals and the inability of ensemble spread to detect errors shared by all seeds.

compute_cost_analysis.subsection_present.reason: Section 8 explicitly discusses training, prediction, structural-feature extraction, uncertainty evaluation, and the ensemble cost tradeoff.
